I am 72 years old. I have farmed this land for 50 years. Let me think about this year the same way I thought about last year, because what worked before will work again.

My 14 mu — I keep about 4 mu for cotton on the sandier piece by the ditch, and the other 10 mu I do wheat and then maize, same as always. This is how my father did it, and how my neighbors do it. If I change too much, I will regret it.

**Wheat (10 mu, winter)** — I plant in early October after the maize is off. I use the improved seed from the agriculture station — the one Old Wang across the road used last year, he got about 500 jin per mu. I buy two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base, and then one bag of urea per mu at the spring greening. That comes to maybe 18 kg of nitrogen per mu. My neighbor uses a bit less but I would rather be safe. A bad wheat harvest means no flour for the family, no money to sell. I irrigate four times from the well — winter water, greening, jointing, and filling. I spray twice for aphids and rust. I use the rotary tiller, my son-in-law hires the machine.

**Maize (10 mu, summer)** — Right after wheat harvest in June, I plant hybrid seed, the Zhengdan type, everyone around here plants it. I apply one bag compound at sowing and topdress urea at the big trumpet stage — about 16 kg N per mu total. Summer rain usually gives water, but I irrigate twice from the well if dry. Spray once for corn borer, maybe twice if I see worms. No-till planting right into the wheat stubble — saves diesel, saves time.

**Cotton (4 mu, spring)** — Cotton eats more fertilizer and more pesticide. Plant hybrid seed in late April. I put down two bags of compound as base and topdress urea twice — about 20 kg N per mu. Cotton needs spraying many times, the bollworm and aphids come again and again — I spray maybe five times through the season. Irrigate three times. Plough deep in spring because cotton roots go down. Last year I got about 250 jin of lint per mu, I hope for the same.

My wife helps, my son works in the city and sends money, so I can afford the fertilizer. I do not gamble with less fertilizer — the cost of wasted fertilizer is small, the cost of a thin harvest is big.
